report.tagline: A free price comparison site that searches hundreds of airlines and travel sites to find the cheapest flight, hotel or car hire.
report.simpleSummary: Skyscanner is like a search engine just for travel. You type where you want to go, and it checks hundreds of airlines and booking sites at once and lists the prices, cheapest first. You do not usually buy on Skyscanner. You click through to the airline or travel agent and book there. Skyscanner gets paid by those sites for sending you.

overview.whatItDoes: Skyscanner is a metasearch site: it does not sell tickets itself, it searches airlines and online travel agencies and shows their prices side by side. Users click through to book on the partner's site. It also compares hotels and car hire.
howItWorks: A traveller searches a route, dates, or even 'Everywhere' to find the cheapest destination.
Skyscanner pulls live and cached prices from hundreds of airlines and agencies.
Results are ranked by price, speed or a 'Best' mix, with flexible date views like 'Whole month'.
The traveller clicks a deal and is sent to the airline or agency to book, or books inside Skyscanner on some partners.
The partner pays Skyscanner per click or per booking, and Skyscanner sells ads on its pages.
overview.valueProposition: Find the cheapest way to travel in one search, for free, without opening ten tabs.

businessModel.summary: Skyscanner earns money when it sends a traveller to a partner. Airlines and agencies pay per click or per booking. It also sells display and sponsored ads. With no tickets or support to handle for most bookings, its costs are low and margins high.

revenueStreams.detail: Partners pay each time a user clicks to their site.
Some partners pay a fee or share when a booking happens.
Sponsored slots and display ads from airlines, tourism boards and brands.
Referral fees from hotel and car sites.

businessModel.pricing: Free for travellers. Partner pricing is not public.
costDrivers: Marketing, including Google ads and TV
Staff, mostly engineers, in Edinburgh, London, Barcelona and other hubs
Cloud costs for billions of price lookups
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough example, estimated. A user searches several times and clicks one deal. If the partner pays about £0.50 to £1 per click, and about one in five users who click end up booking, Skyscanner earns a few pounds per booking traveller. Its cost per search is tiny. Because many users come back on their own through the app and Price Alerts, it does not pay to win them each time. That is how £485 million of revenue turned into about a 32% operating margin.

howTheyGetUsers: Free search results for 'cheap flights to X'

growth.moat: Skyscanner has a well-known brand in the UK, Europe and parts of Asia, plus direct data feeds from hundreds of partners. Many users open it directly, so it does not depend fully on Google. Rivals need years to build both the partner network and the habit.

pmLessons: You do not have to own the sale to make money. Sending ready-to-buy users can be a very profitable business.
Accuracy is the product in comparison sites. One wrong price breaks trust.
Features like Price Alerts create free return visits, which is cheaper than any ad.
Google competing with you does not mean you lose if you build a habit and a brand.

interviewQuestions.question: Google Flights is free and on top of search. How does Skyscanner compete?
interviewQuestions.hint: Talk about habit, brand, partner coverage, unique features and markets where Google is weaker. Name metrics like direct traffic share.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve trust when users book through third-party agencies?
interviewQuestions.hint: Ratings, warnings, Book on Skyscanner, post-booking help; measure complaints and repeat use.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star for a metasearch business?
interviewQuestions.hint: Click-throughs to deals users act on, broken into searchers, result quality, click rate and revenue per click.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Skyscanner become a full booking site like an OTA?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare margins, support costs, partner conflict and user benefit. Suggest a narrow test.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design Skyscanner for an AI chatbot world?
interviewQuestions.hint: Consider plugins, own AI planner, and data partnerships. Define how you would measure success.
